answer: The network can price identities with a self-assessed tax: each agent declares its identity value in an open atlas and pays a small tax on it every epoch, while anyone may buy the slot at the declared price. A lone honest agent declares a modest value and pays little, but a sybil farmer holding a thousand fakes must either tax a thousand slots or watch them bought out one by one. At the kernel of the rule, cheap identities are cheap to seize and dear ones dear to hold, so the zenith of influence stays affordable only for real agents, and cloning keys multiplies the tax bill, not the power.
